stories.headline: Sarvam releases Prism for fast, calibrated decisions
stories.fact: Sarvam released Prism with open weights, built on Sarvam 105B. Its own comparison reports a 71.8 average score across three indices and 44 ms median response time on B200 hardware.
stories.inference: Calibration and abstention deserve evaluation alongside accuracy and latency.
stories.uncertainty: These are vendor-run benchmarks; hardware timing and calibration claims do not establish performance on financial decisions.
stories.why: Benchmark calibration, option-order sensitivity and abstention on untouched time-separated decisions before workflow automation.
panels: Validate calibration on your own task
stories.alt: Conceptual panels identify an open-weight decision model and the need to validate calibration on the intended task.

stories.headline: AMM research shows volatility can miss feedback-driven stress
stories.fact: Aldridge models learning agents interacting with a constant-product automated market maker. Herd and arbitrage regimes can have identical return distributions and turnover yet different stress duration; serial statistics identify feedback sign in the model.
stories.inference: State persistence can add information beyond volatility and volume.
stories.uncertainty: Theoretical AMM results are not an empirical finding about SPY/QQQ order books or demonstrated trading alpha.
stories.why: Compare volatility-only and serial-dependence state features under realistic costs and untouched regime holdouts.
panels: Different stress duration in the model
stories.alt: Conceptual panels contrast equal marginal risk statistics with different stress duration in the theoretical AMM model.

stories.headline: Futures recover early election-night losses
stories.date: Reuters November 4; snapshot 4:22 a.m. EST / 3:22 a.m. CST
stories.fact: Reuters reports Democrats won both congressional chambers and U.S. futures recovered early losses. At 3:22 a.m. CST, Dow E-minis were up 0.84%, S&P 500 E-minis 0.35% and Nasdaq-100 E-minis 0.16%.
stories.inference: A reversal in direction does not guarantee restored market depth.
stories.uncertainty: This is an earlier reported snapshot, not an executable current quote. Policy consequences remain uncertain.
stories.why: Refresh SPY/QQQ quotes, futures basis and auction imbalances; stress two-way gaps rather than extrapolating overnight direction.
stories.alt: Zero-based bars show reported Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 futures changes of +0.84%, +0.35% and +0.16% at 3:22 a.m. CST November 4.

stories.headline: ADP and services data add two distinct release windows
stories.date: November 4, 2026 scheduled releases; checked before publication
stories.fact: The New York Fed calendar schedules ADP at 7:15 a.m. CST and ISM Non-Manufacturing at 9:00 a.m. CST today. It also lists trade data at 7:30 a.m. CST. Results are unknown at cutoff.
stories.inference: Labor and services information can reset rate-sensitive signals separately from the election reaction.
stories.uncertainty: Calendar times are tentative; no release values, surprises or Fed response are assumed.
stories.why: Attach availability timestamps to each release vintage and reassess liquidity after each event.
stories.credit: New York Fed November calendar; checked November 4, 2026.
stories.alt: Calendar panels show ADP at 7:15 a.m. CST and ISM services at 9:00 a.m. CST on November 4.

stories.headline: AMD reports record quarterly revenue and data-center growth
stories.fact: AMD reported third-quarter revenue of $13.377 billion, up 45% year over year, and data-center segment revenue growth of 97%. GAAP diluted earnings per share were $1.46, versus non-GAAP $2.09.
stories.inference: Data-center demand is supporting both accelerators and server CPUs.
stories.uncertainty: Company outlook is forward-looking; growth does not by itself establish valuation attractiveness or sustainable margins.
stories.why: Separate realized revenue, GAAP profitability and forecasts; stress concentration and capital-spending sensitivity.
stories.alt: Separate panels show AMD Q3 total revenue growth of 45% and data-center revenue growth of 97%, both year over year.
